substitutions.why: the Dart package name; the analyzer fails without it, so this is the one substitution the compiler also checks
the application id, in manifests, Gradle, entitlements, xcconfigs and the bundle-id whitelist

path_moves.why: the Java and Kotlin source package; a move, not a content substitution, so `--exact` resolves the base blob through it

names_the_needle_why: files that may spell the needle on purpose, so the forward check exempts them: the CI workflow that *runs* the sweep documents what it looks for, which is the same reason docs/rebase-runbook.md says `package:Kelivo/` — a swept record asserts the opposite of what happened, and this one is inside the scanned roots

l10n.why: the keys whose string names the other application because it describes *that* product: the two backup-target labels, and the two v1.3.7 strings that walk a reader through the official toolbox converting a foreign backup into a Kelivo archive. The archive those strings describe really is Kelivo's, so renaming it would make the string false — the same reasoning the protected list uses for `kelivo.psycheas.top`

protected.name: com.psyche.kelivo
protected.why: the *previous* application id, which is a filesystem identity rather than branding: kelivo_file_uri's whitelist resolves the macOS container and Windows AppData paths this fork wrote before the rename, so the old id has to stay beside the new one. A sweep turns it into a second `com.cuplivo.cuplivo`, the set stays syntactically valid and the analyzer sees nothing, while every path recorded by an older install silently stops resolving

protected.name: kelivo://
protected.why: the workspace content scheme: persisted in tab state and in every kelivo://workspace|chat|session|skills|tmp|mounts URL

protected.name: kelivo-file:
protected.why: the portable attachment URI scheme; every archived image and file reference in a backup is one

protected.name: uri\.scheme == 'kelivo'
protected.why: the scheme *value* the accept side compares against, twice: the host check and the scope's owns(). The constructing side (`replace(scheme: 'kelivo')`) is what it has to agree with, so pinning only the literal's total count is not enough — this pair is what a sweep that renames one side and not the other breaks, and it made every workspace page load return null while the analyzer stayed clean
